Preprocessing prepares collected media for analysis. This includes deciding which images and video frames become observations, keeping links to the original posts, and extracting written or spoken text where it helps answer the research question. Converting visual material into text enables established text-analysis methods [@Baden2022-oe], while retaining images allows us to study visual content directly.

For winter 2026/27, use the following workflow:

1. Import the collection and check metadata and local media.
2. [Select gallery images and sample video frames](frame-sampling.qmd) according to the research question.
3. Inspect the visual sample and retain an image-level table before starting [image analysis](../image-analysis/index.qmd).
4. Add OCR and audio transcription when the analysis also requires written or spoken content.

## Import a Current Tidal Tales Export

Start with the [Tidal Tales import notebook](../notebooks/tidaltales-import.ipynb) when using a current CSV export. It maps TikTok metadata to the `df_posts` table expected below, checks local media, and prepares the `posts/images/<author>/<id>.jpg` and `posts/videos/<author>/<id>.<extension>` layout. Keep the exported CSV and the downloaded `tidaltales/` directory together; the CSV alone contains no media.

The notebook makes duplicate handling explicit and saves a media manifest, including missing files and all gallery-image references. The compatibility export uses one representative image per post for the older OCR loop. Follow its handoff instructions to set the paths in the preprocessing notebook and retain the actual image filename in the Text Master.

## Sample Images and Video Frames

The [image and frame sampling chapter](frame-sampling.qmd) compares fixed time intervals, a fixed number of frames per video, random selection within time intervals, and shot-based strategies. It introduces a pilot workflow and an image-level table linking each selected frame to its post and timestamp. Covers and first frames remain useful for specific questions, but are not the default representation of an entire video.

For galleries, retain the individual images and their order. The import notebook's one-image compatibility export is intended for the older OCR loop; use the full media manifest for the visual workflow.

## OCR & Whisper

### Earlier text-extraction workflow

The embedded 2024 notebook below is retained for its OCR and transcription examples. Its post-level image handling does not preserve results for multiple frames or gallery images from the same post. ## Next Steps

Retain the original media, the post table, and the image-level sampling record. Check extraction quality and sampling coverage before interpreting automated results. Continue with [visual exploration](../image-analysis/exploration.qmd) and [classification](../image-analysis/classification.qmd), or use extracted text in the [text-analysis workflow](index.qmd).
